findings.title: Backup-code consumption is vulnerable to concurrent replay
findings.body: This read-modify-write sequence is not atomic: two login requests can both read the same stored code, both find it, and both authenticate before either update is visible. Concurrent use of different codes can also overwrite one another and restore a code that was already consumed. Since backup codes are promised to work exactly once, consume them with an atomic conditional update or transaction/lock so only one request can succeed.

findings.title: The external-provider 2FA flow does not offer backup-code recovery
findings.body: When OAuth or SAML login redirects to the `totpEmail` flow, this conditional renders `ExternalTotpFooter` instead of `TwoFactorFooter`, so users never see the new “Lost access” option or a backup-code input. This can affect users whose account has 2FA enabled when its identity provider changes; even if the UI offered recovery, `authorize` also rejects a non-CAL user's request without `totpCode` before reaching the backup-code branch. Such users cannot use their backup codes to sign in.
